#### 1. Joubert syndrome 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.776)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:25018)

**Proposed mechanism:** TMEM216 (HGNC:25018) —LEADS_TO→ Ciliary dysfunction (HP:0034247); Ciliary dysfunction (HP:0034247) —LEADS_TO→ Joubert syndrome (HP:0001290); Ciliary dysfunction (HP:0034247) —LEADS_TO→ Meckel syndrome (HP:0011027). Loss-of-function mutations in TMEM216 lead to general ciliary dysfunction, which is a core feature underlying both Joubert syndrome and Meckel syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with loss-of-function mutations in TMEM216 who do not exhibit features of either Joubert syndrome or Meckel syndrome, or conversely, identification of individuals with these conditions caused by mutations in entirely different genes with no overlap in TMEM216 function. _(variant: gnomAD v2.1.1 shows no loss-of-function variants in TMEM216, consistent with its pathogenic role.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TMEM216 in both syndromes could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting ciliary function that benefit patients with either condition.
